contract: An analyzer can return an owned diagnostic that is included in the compilation result.
Analyzers receive the syntax trees after generated sources have been added.
Generated source output is owned and participates in normal JavaScript emission.
Authored imports can resolve and type-check against generated exports.
Each generator reads the same immutable authored syntax-tree and diagnostic snapshot; earlier generator output is excluded from later generator inputs.
Every registered generator runs before the analyzer stage begins.
Generated files are emitted in generator registration order and per-generator output order.
Analyzer diagnostics with equal spans retain analyzer registration order.
Owned generator diagnostics are included in the compilation result.
Owned analyzer diagnostics are included in the compilation result.
Generated files pass through the regular compiler checker and can report TS2322.
Each compile call owns a fresh generated syntax-tree and output set.
A generated source that collides with an authored path is rejected or reported.
Multiple generated sources with the same path are rejected or reported.
An unsupported generated-source extension is rejected and reported.
Generated sources that resolve outside the compilation root are diagnosed and excluded from emit.
